title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 9/10: "We'll learn from it and hopefully be better for it"
headline: A.J. Brown left the game with a reported high ankle sprain; Vrabel gave no firm timeline and will update next week, so his availability is uncertain.
summary: Vrabel said A.J. Brown did not finish the preseason game and that the team is still running tests, so there is no confirmed diagnosis or timeline yet. He said he doesn't know whether Brown will be available for the coming week and promised an update next week, with the treatment plan to follow once the reports are in. Other returners Morgan Moses, Hunter Henry and Carlton Davis came back after bumps and bruises, and nobody else is expected to miss time. Vrabel defended the joint-practice reps, saying the backups' limited preseason snaps wouldn't have prepared the team for the environment. He attributed Drake Maye's last-throw issue to timing and protection, said Maye will learn from it, and said he expects Maye to keep playing at a high level. On the run game, Vrabel said the team ran better in the second half and protected better, though not well enough. He credited Gabe Jacas with continued improvement, especially his instinctive red-zone tackle. Corey Kiner got more offensive involvement while TreVeyon Henderson is still learning the offense, and Vrabel said Kiner has worked hard and will get more chances to run.

Vrabel said the team practices ball security daily and expects receivers, backs and the QB to protect the ball, though the turnover issues need to stop becoming a pattern.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 9/9: “We never accept losing, but we have to embrace moving on"
headline: Patriots lost the Week 1 opener at Seattle after three Drake Maye interceptions and a failed late drive; Vrabel stressed turnovers and fourth-quarter execution, and expressed confidence in Maye.
summary: Vrabel said New England didn't win the game in the second half, where it failed to make plays in critical situations. He called turnovers a broken record and said the team has to avoid giving the ball away and create more of its own. He credited the offense for battling back on fourth down and the defense for early stops, and said the team handled the road environment well enough, aside from a punt-team penalty and a false start. On the quarterback, he said the team has complete confidence in Drake Maye and that he will make many plays, while acknowledging three interceptions can't happen. He defended the late-game approach, saying the team wanted to be aggressive without being reckless, and that the third-and-long calls against heavy coverage made punting a possibility. On the defense, he said a fourth-down big play came from missed tackles and that Seattle's run defense (second in the league last year) made running hard. He said the team was not caught off guard by Seattle's blitzes and that it hit back, and that it has to move on and improve over a long season. He said he had no update on an injured player who was unable to return.

injuries.detail: Coach had no update on a player who was unable to return to the game; the name is garbled in the captions, so the player cannot be confirmed.

signals.claim: Needs to cut down turnovers; coach says the team cannot keep throwing interceptions.
signals.note: Three interceptions in the opener is a concern for his fantasy floor, though Vrabel publicly backed him.
signals.quote: you can't throw three interceptions. You know Drake knows that.

topics.detail: Vrabel said Seattle was second in the league in run defense last year and likely picked up where it left off. He also said Seattle blitzed often, including blitz-zero looks similar to those in the Super Bowl, but that New England was not caught off guard.

A punt-team issue and a false start were noted as mistakes. Vrabel also said the team could not end every possession with a kick and that the late third-and-long situations were hard against heavy coverage.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Recaps The Week 1 Win vs. Patriots
headline: Sam Darnold's hip-area muscle injury remains unclear with no new update, while Drew Lock was praised for his poise in the Week 1 comeback win and Julian Love, Byron Murphy, and Nehemiah Pritchett drew strong reviews.
summary: Macdonald said there was no new update on Sam Darnold beyond positive feelings, that the team is still working out the extent of the hip-area muscle injury, and that a clearer plan should be set by Monday. He said Darnold was back in the building and that they had texted but not yet met in person. On the pre-snap penalties, he said the issues were multiple small causes rather than one fixable problem, so the fix is a return to fundamentals in practice, call entry, and motion and shifts. He was excited about the run game, saying runners were decisive and the team cut negative runs, though keeping drives alive would create more carries. He praised Drew Lock's play in relief, calling the ball never in jeopardy and saying he prepares like a starter. Macdonald highlighted rookie Jadarian Price's runs, Jalen Sundell's blocking, Nehemiah Pritchett, Julian Love (possibly his best game as a Seahawk), and Byron Murphy as standouts. He said Trevon Diggs was inactive and that his return timing is uncertain, while Rodney Thomas II stepped up in the secondary. He also said the defense's front flexibility and the offense's identity under Brian Fleury remain consistent with the Seahawks' system despite new play calls and language.
